answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through repeated, bonded participation: each account locks a scarce token, then gains influence gradually as independent peers attest to its useful work across many rounds. A sudden tide of fresh identities cannot instantly sway decisions; each must post its own bond and build a track record, while misconduct forfeits the stake. The crystal-clear cost is capital locked per identity, plus time and effort to earn attestations; coordinated accounts also risk a ripple of losses if their fraud is exposed.
